title: A Global Picture of Molecular Changes Associated to LPS Treatment in THP-1 Derived Human Macrophages by Fourier Transform Infrared Microspectroscopy
authors: Diletta Ami; Ana Rita Franco; Valentina Artusa; Paolo Mereghetti; Francesco Peri; Antonino Natalello
abstract: Fourier transform infrared microspectroscopy analyzed THP-1 derived macrophages treated with LPS. The study identified spectral markers in lipids, proteins, and sulfated sugars, highlighting their role in inflammation.

title: Macrophage Polarization: Different Gene Signatures in M1(LPS+) vs. Classically and M2(LPS–) vs. Alternatively Activated Macrophages
authors: Marco Orecchioni, Yanal Ghosheh, Akula Bala Pramod, Klaus Ley
abstract: This study compared gene expression in *in vivo* M1/M2 macrophages with *in vitro* classically/alternatively activated macrophages. The findings indicate that *in vivo* M1/M2 polarization is not equivalent to *in vitro* activation states.

title: Lipopolysaccharide-mediated macrophage polarization, conserved pathogenesis, and implications for peripheral neuropathy: a systematic review
authors: Leah Elson; Niels Eijkelkamp; J. Henk Coert
abstract: This systematic review synthesized evidence for a conserved lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-mediated pathogenic mechanism across diverse tissues and evaluated its potential relevance to peripheral neuropathy

title: RNA-Binding Proteins in the Control of LPS-Induced Macrophage Response
authors: Dirk H. Ostareck, Antje Ostareck-Lederer

abstract: This review examines RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) like TTP, HUR, TIAR, and hnRNP K in LPS-induced macrophage responses. These RBPs globally regulate inflammation-related gene expression, impacting signaling and cytokine production.

authors: Jie Deng; Chunmei Wen; Xiangyu Ding; Xi Zhang; Guoqing Hou; Andong Liu; Hui Xu; Xuan Cao; Yongheng B...
abstract: High-throughput phosphoproteomics identified novel mediators of LPS-induced signaling in mouse macrophages. LKB1-MARK2 signaling was found to regulate the production of key inflammatory cytokines.

authors: Hyesook Lee, Jung-Hwa Han, Kangbin An, Yun Jeong Kang, Hyun Hwangbo, Ji Hye Heo, Byung Hyun Choi, Ja...
abstract: Recombinant human KAI1/CD82 was studied for its effect on LPS-stimulated macrophages. It attenuates M1 macrophage polarization by blocking the TLR4/JNK/NF-κB pathway.

title: Lipopolysaccharide-Activated Macrophages Suppress Cellular Senescence and Promote Rejuvenation in Human Dermal Fibroblasts
authors: Hiroyuki Inagawa; Chie Kohchi; Miyuki Uehiro; Gen-Ichiro Soma
abstract: LPS-activated macrophages were studied for their effect on senescent human dermal fibroblasts. Their secretions suppressed senescence and partially rejuvenated aged fibroblasts.

title: Comparative Study of The Effect of LPS on The Function of BALB/c and C57BL/6 Peritoneal Macrophages
authors: Sara Soudi; Ahmad Zavaran-Hosseini; Zuhair Muhammad Hassan; Masoud Soleimani; Fatemeh Jamshidi Adega...
abstract: Peritoneal macrophages from BALB/c and C57BL/6 mice were stimulated with LPS to compare their responses. Different mouse strains exhibit distinct cytokine profiles and functional activities when exposed to LPS.

title: Transmembrane TNFα-Expressed Macrophage Membrane-Coated Chitosan Nanoparticles as Cancer Therapeutics
authors: Srirupa Bhattacharyya; Siddhartha Sankar Ghosh
abstract: Macrophage membranes expressing TNFα were used to coat chitosan nanoparticles. These nanoparticles showed significant anti-cancer effects and good biocompatibility.

authors: Gen-Ichiro Soma; Masataka Oda; Vindy Tjendana Tjhin; Chie Kohchi; Hiroyuki Inagawa
id: Matched: Regulation of innate immunity by LPS as an environmental agent
abstract: Oral and transdermal LPS administration was studied for its effects on self-healing. This method safely enhances healing through a "macrophage network" involving mucosal immune cells.

title: Lipopolysaccharide from Porphyromonas gingivalis, but Not from Porphyromonas endodontalis, Induces Macrophage M1 Profile
authors: Pablo Veloso; Alejandra Fernández; Jessica Astorga; David González-Quintanilla; Alfredo Castro; Alej...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of lipopolysaccharides from *Porphyromonas gingivalis* and *Porphyromonas endodontalis* on macrophage polarization. *P. gingivalis* LPS induced an M1 macrophage profile, while *P. endodontalis* LPS did not.

authors: Akane Tanaka, Joyce To, Bronwyn O’Brien, Sheila Donnelly, Maria Lund
abstract: This study assessed the stability of eight common reference genes in LPS-stimulated murine macrophages. It found that some traditional genes are unreliable, and identified two new, stable reference genes for accurate gene expression analysis.

abstract: This study analyzed GPCR expression in mouse macrophages, comparing it to other cell types and LPS-stimulated macrophages. Several P2RY family members showed macrophage-specific expression or LPS-regulated changes, suggesting roles in macrophage biology and inflammation.

title: MARCO is an IFN-restricted immunometabolic decoy LPS receptor
authors: Shriram Ramani, Sara Cahill, Matthew Finnegan, Laurel Stine, Liraz Shmuel-Galia, Fiachra Humphries *
abstract: MARCO was identified as a macrophage decoy LPS receptor that restrains caspase 11 activity. Its expression is regulated by itaconate and NRF2, with IFN impairing this regulation to control inflammasome activation.
